title: CRASH-052: std read property stack tmp member escapes into get suar (stack-use-after-return)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:stack-use-after-return at Zend/zend_execute.c:59 in zend_pzval_lock_func when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 3d7b0bab28e7, which postdates the release, and names the defect at Zend/zend_execute.c:1138 (declaration) / :1146-1149 (escape) in zend_fetch_property_address_read; claimed Zend/zend_object_handlers.c:277 is a real sibling instance of the same idiom but is not reached by this trigger
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing. Needs: ASAN_OPTIONS detect_stack_use_after_return=1.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has zend_pzval_lock_func at Zend/zend_execute.c:59 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #0); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites
